facts.d: Directions issued to do complete justice bind the parties and can operate as law of the land until the legislature acts — but they carry no precedential value. A power that makes law without making precedent.

facts.t: Forty per cent of Article 142 invocations are ambiguous
facts.d: An IIM Ahmedabad study of 1,579 Supreme Court cases citing Article 142 or complete justice found the usage unclear in almost two-fifths of them — invoked without explaining what the provision was doing in the reasoning.

facts.t: 2024 set a record for suo motu cases
facts.d: Twelve in a single year, the highest ever. Article 32 and 226 jurisdiction combined with the growth of public interest litigation has steadily widened what the constitutional courts will take up on their own motion.

bank.e: They may operate as law of the land until the legislature or executive acts, but they set no precedent.

bank.q: With reference to SCBA v. UoI (1998), consider the following statements:
s: Article 142 was described as a valuable weapon to prevent clogging of the stream of injustice.
The Court held that Article 142 may supplement but not supplant substantive law.
It held that Article 142 can override express statutory prohibitions at will.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The supplement-not-supplant formula is precisely the limit the Court drew.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (use of Article 142):
bank.e: Union Carbide on compensation, Lakshmi Kant Pandey on adoptions, Reliance as the criticised contract case, and SaveLIFE on road safety.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a recognised method of exercising suo motu jurisdiction?
o: Acting against a person showing contempt
Transferring a case to itself or to a lower court
Taking cognisance of a pressing issue affecting society
Reviewing a Bill before it receives presidential assent
bank.e: India has no pre-assent reference power exercisable by the court on its own motion — that is the Irish model under Article 26.

bank.as: Suo motu jurisdiction is criticised as producing selective justice.
bank.rs: Which matters are taken up depends on the priorities of individual judges.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — alongside the procedural concern that such proceedings may lack proper notice and hearing.

bank.q: Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan (2014) held that for a direction to be effective there must be:
bank.e: An implementation mechanism — a direction without machinery to enforce it achieves nothing.

bank.q: Consider the following criticisms of Article 142:
s: The Coal Block allocation cancellations of 2014 created legal uncertainty.
The Reliance Natural Resources decision was criticised as effectively rewriting a contract.
Its exercise is subject to appeal before a larger bench as of right.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. There is no appeal as of right — the absence of a check is itself part of the criticism.

bank.q: All of the following are cited examples of suo motu intervention EXCEPT:
bank.e: The Bhopal settlement was an Article 142 exercise in pending proceedings, not a suo motu initiation.

bank.q: Who observed that the greatest danger to the administration of justice arises from judges' genuine desire to do justice in each individual case?
bank.e: H. M. Seervai — the classic warning against equity untethered from law.

bank.q: With reference to the growth of suo motu jurisdiction, consider the following:
s: Articles 32 and 226 supply its constitutional footing.
The expansion of public interest litigation widened its scope.
2024 saw the highest number of suo motu cases on record.
bank.e: All three are correct — twelve suo motu matters in 2024.
